title: Renaming node or file makes it lose focus on Linux
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible on linux in v4.6.1.stable.arch_linux [14d19694e]
Godot v4.6.1.stable (14d19694e) - Arch Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Mon, 09 Feb 2026 17:16:33 +0000 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - AMD Radeon 780M Graphics (radeonsi, phoenix, LLVM 21.1.6, DRM 3.64, 6.18.9-arch1-2) - AMD Ryzen 7 8745HS w/ Radeon 780M Graphics (16 threads) - 28.18 GiB memory


Not reproducible on windows 11 VM with v4.6.1.stable.official [14d19694e]
Godot v4.6.1.stable - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - integrated Microsoft Basic Render Driver (Microsoft; 10.0.26100.5074) - AMD Ryzen 7 8745HS w/ Radeon 780M Graphics (2 threads) - 3.99 GiB memory

### System information

Godot v4.6.1.stable (14d19694e) - Arch Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Mon, 09 Feb 2026 17:16:33 +0000 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - AMD Radeon 780M Graphics (radeonsi, phoenix, LLVM 21.1.6, DRM 3.64, 6.18.9-arch1-2) - AMD Ryzen 7 8745HS w/ Radeon 780M Graphics (16 threads) - 28.18 GiB memory

### Issue description

On linux, renaming a node in the scene tree causes the tree to lose focus. This means you can't rename, then add a child.

The same happens when renaming in the file system dialoge (Might be related to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/102051)

After making hyperland focus a different wind (by moving the mouse over the other window) and moving the mouse back to godot, the node in the scene tree is focused again.

Even the ctrl + s shortcut to save doesn't work until after tabbing out and back in.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4dd9d32a-85a0-4baa-b994-d428b25464ce

### Steps to reproduce

1. Select a node in the scene tree
2. Use the rename hotkey (F2)
3. Type a new name and press enter
4. Try to press F2 again or Ctrl+a to add a new node, and notice the scene tree isn't focused
5. Move the mouse out of the godot window, then back into it
6. Now using Ctrl+a does work
